subject: Hotpath surge: fallback playbook, short-term mitigations & roadmap questions
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@clearcart.com>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@clearcart.com
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:10:00 -0500
Subject: Sharp latency spike on storefront hotpath (tokenization -> gen API)

Grace —

We're seeing a sustained p95 jump on our checkout completion path starting ~08:55 ET. Requests hit the gen API and stall for 800-1,200ms more than usual; throughput to our service has also dropped by ~35% despite stable client QPS. This is impacting cart conversions.

We're running the r-32 model pinned at v1.12 with the default routing policy. Logs attached include a short CPU sample and the client-side traces. Any quick mitigation you can advise would be amazing.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Director of Platform Engineering | ClearCart
Attachments: cpu-sample-09-10.txt
From: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@clearcart.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:23:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Sharp latency spike on storefront hotpath (tokenization -> gen API)

Team — forwarding ClearCart impact. Key asks:
- Immediate: triage and get a short-term mitigation we can apply without a model rollback. Customer is seeing conversion loss.
- Near-term: confirm whether this is a scheduling/queueing issue vs kernel regression vs model-side kv cache eviction.
- Product/roadmap: if this becomes a recurring pattern, what config knobs do we need exposed to customers to avoid this? (routing weight floor, model-weighted routing, faster failover to a slim variant?)

Soojin / Karthik, can you start with the runtime traces and the CPU sample attached? Marcus / Marissa, FYI on product trade-offs and customer communication. I want a short customer-facing summary we can send by 10:30 ET.

Grace Oconnor
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0147
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena@clearcart.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:38:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Sharp latency spike on storefront hotpath (tokenization -> gen API)

Quick findings (first-pass):
- Runtime traces show a burst of longer kernel queues on the r-32 path coincident with an uptick in long-seq requests from a single customer shard (ClearCart).
- CPU samples show elevated scheduler W-AI wait times and frequent kernel preemption at the same PIDs. Not seeing obvious OOMs or disk stalls.
- KV-cache hit-rate for ClearCart's prefix set dropped ~18% at 08:54 — looks like a cache churn event.

Short-term mitigations I recommend (safe to apply now):
1) Apply routing override to steer ClearCart cold traffic to r-16-slim variant (compatible and validated) for next 30m.
2) Temporarily increase per-customer concurrency cap to allow controlled burst smoothing (from 12->16) so request queues don't back up.
3) Kick a targeted KV warmup for the affected prefixes.

I can roll 1) and 2) from the control plane now; will need Marcus to sign off on the product-visible cap change and Karthik to coordinate the warmup script. I'll attach the trace snippets to INF-2248.

- Soojin
Soojin Lee | Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: trace-snippets.tar.gz (referenced)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena@clearcart.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:51:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Sharp latency spike on storefront hotpath (tokenization -> gen API)

Agree with Soojin's mitigations. A couple product notes:
- Steer-to-slim will reduce cost per token but may change tokenization edge-cases — we should document the functional delta and flag it in the customer note.
- Increasing concurrency cap is an exception we can allow for ClearCart for 30m, but we should gate the API-level knob behind a guardrail so it isn't abused. Proposal: an account-level temporary override feature with an expiry and audit log.

Karthik — can you run the warmup script and validate no regressions on the slim model for the recent prompt sets? We should capture a quick microbenchmark. If warmup and steering succeed, I'll prepare a small product follow-up (low-effort) to expose an account-level emergency routing toggle in the console.

Marcus Lin
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime & Routing
From: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@clearcart.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 11:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Sharp latency spike on storefront hotpath (tokenization -> gen API)

Elena — quick update and next steps (short customer note):

What happened: we detected a hotpath latency surge tied to a temporary KV-cache churn that coincided with an influx of long-sequence requests from ClearCart's shard. This created longer kernel queues and a knock-on throughput drop.

What we did (applied):
- Steered ClearCart traffic for the affected prefixes to a validated slim variant (r-16-slim) for 30 minutes to relieve kernel scheduling pressure.
- Increased the account concurrency cap from 12 to 16 for a 30-minute window to allow smoother burst handling.
- Triggered a targeted KV warmup for your recent prefixes.

What you'll see: slightly different tokenization edge behavior while on r-16-slim (we validated core prompt outputs). We expect conversion latency to recover within ~5-10 minutes; we'll confirm with you when p95 returns to baseline.

Product/next steps (internal):
- INF-2248: Soojin documented traces and attached logs; Karthik to run a microbenchmark on r-16-slim (ETA 30m).
- Marcus will scope an account-level emergency routing toggle and a guarded concurrency override (roadmap/backlog).
- Marissa to draft the post-incident product note and update the public routing FAQ for emergency steering lanes.

Attachments: fallback-routing-config.patch (applied), cpu-sample-09-10.txt (from your team).

If recovery stalls, we'll open a bridge and escalate to kernel engineering.

Thanks for the quick report — we'll ping when p95 is back down.

Best,
Grace Oconnor
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0147
